N4_counterexample.purpose: Counterexample outside N=4m+2; the congruence hypothesis is essential.

proof_lemmas.full_support: A fixed-point-free involutive cycle automorphism is an edge-axis reflection or the half-turn. Every edge-axis reflection has exactly two adjacent matched pairs.
proof_lemmas.halfturn_exclusion: For p(j)=j+n and odd n, J=P_M D is an orthogonal complex structure. A commutes with J and e^A=J=iI on the induced complex vector space. The antipodal permutation has no cycle-edge support, so tr_R(JA)=0; also tr_R(A)=0, hence tr_C(A)=0. But the n complex eigenphases are theta_l=pi/2+2*pi*k_l, so their sum is pi/2*(n+4K), which cannot vanish for odd n.
proof_lemmas.proper_support: Every component is an even path and the fixed-point-free path automorphism is reversal. Each component contributes its central adjacent matched pair. If there is only one component, it spans all N vertices and its endpoint pair across the unique missing cycle edge is a second adjacent matched pair.
proof_lemmas.support_graph: A commutes with exp(A)=P_M D, so conjugation by the signed permutation preserves the nonzero-edge support graph. Since exp(A) is block diagonal over support components and is a signed permutation, the matching permutation preserves each component.

scope_limit: The separator applies only to physically reachable signed perfect-matching atoms and their positive mixtures. It is not proved for arbitrary cycle exponentials Q=exp(A(c))D, so the full physical convex-hull problem remains open.
theorem: Every perfect-matching atom R_M=P_M D that equals exp(A(c)) for a real skew generator supported on the N-cycle has at least two matching edges that are cycle edges.
